key_insight: To understand why language-model data attribution fails, evaluations need to separate the effects of different dataset properties. This paper introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) to support that diagnosis through fact tracing.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations change multiple dataset properties at once, making it difficult to determine why a method succeeds or fails at linking a model’s factual outputs to its training data.
method: Explore the design space of language-model data attribution, focusing on evaluation.
Introduce CATT as a controlled benchmark for tracing facts back to training data.
Use controlled evaluation to investigate attribution failures; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify the full experimental setup or results.
impact: More diagnostic evaluations could help practitioners distinguish attribution-method weaknesses from dataset effects, supporting better method selection and development.
visual_elements: Tracing diagram: training documents → language model → factual answer, with attribution arrows back to source documents.
Side-by-side comparison: evaluations with multiple changing properties versus controlled evaluations.
Dataset-property sliders illustrating how individual factors can be varied.
Diagnostic magnifying-glass icon linking attribution failures to potential causes.
paper_title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
paper_authors: Steven Yu, Sheng-Yu Wang, Kimia Hamidieh, Antonio Torralba, David Bau
